gloss: drawing a sword; unsheathing a blade

definitions.gloss: drawing a sword; unsheathing a blade
definitions.explanation: The act of pulling a sword from its scabbard, especially as a technique in Japanese martial arts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{素早|すばや}く→素早い：17093_subayai⟧{抜刀|ばっとう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
{抜刀|ばっとう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{構|かま}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}った→取る：00565_toru⟧。

{抜刀術|ばっとうじゅつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{鞘|さや}→鞘：14698_saya⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{刀|かたな}→刀：02194_katana⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧⟦{瞬間|しゅんかん}→瞬間：03226_shunkan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{斬|き}りつける⟦{武術|ぶじゅつ}→武術：13244_bujutsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Battōjutsu is a martial art in which one strikes at the moment of drawing the blade from its scabbard.

notes:
A compound of {抜|ばつ} (to draw out) and {刀|とう} (sword). This term is closely associated with Japanese swordsmanship traditions. The art of drawing and cutting in one motion is called {抜刀術|ばっとうじゅつ} or {居合|いあい} (iaido), and is still practiced as a martial art today.

The word frequently appears in historical dramas (⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧), manga, anime, and games featuring samurai themes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抜刀|ばっとう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to draw a sword
- {抜刀術|ばっとうじゅつ}: the art of drawing and cutting
- {抜刀|ばっとう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{構|かま}え: sword-drawing stance
- {抜刀隊|ばっとうたい}: sword-drawing unit (historical military term)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {居合|いあい}: iaido (the art/way of drawing the sword; more emphasis on the spiritual discipline)
- {納刀|のうとう}: sheathing the sword (the opposite action)
- {帯刀|たいとう}: wearing a sword at one's side
